actions.justification: Mandatory Hour-1 Bundle: Measure serum lactate immediately to confirm severity of septic shock and guide resuscitation. Patient has MAP 60 and SpO2 88%, consistent with severe sepsis/shock.
Mandatory Hour-1 Bundle: Obtain blood cultures BEFORE administering antibiotics to identify causative organism and guide targeted therapy.

Mandatory Hour-1 Bundle: Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics immediately after blood cultures are drawn. SSC guidelines recommend antibiotic administration within 1 hour of septic shock recognition (strong recommendation).

MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle: administer 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid for hypotension (BP 80/50, MAP 60). Patient has HFrEF EF 15% so monitor closely for fluid overload, but this is guideline-mandated and must not be withheld.

MAP is 60 mmHg (target ≥65). SSC guidelines recommend norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor in septic shock. Given severe cardiomyopathy (EF 15%), vasopressor support is critical to maintain perfusion pressure without over-relying on fluid boluses.

Patient has confusion, hypoxia (SpO2 88%), hypotension, tachycardia, and CKD — multi-organ dysfunction is likely. Formal organ dysfunction assessment guides further management including ICU transfer and organ-specific interventions.

Patient remains hemodynamically unstable (MAP 60, BP 80/50, HR 105, SpO2 88%). Serial vital sign reassessment is critical to evaluate response to ongoing vasopressor and fluid resuscitation, and to guide further interventions.

BMP is essential to assess renal function (patient has CKD stage 3), electrolytes, glucose, and bicarbonate. Will help evaluate metabolic acidosis severity, guide fluid management, and monitor for AKI progression in the setting of septic shock.

Patient has HFrEF (EF 15%), leg edema, worsening dyspnea, and SpO2 88%. CXR will help identify pulmonary edema vs. pneumonia as infection source, and guide cautious fluid management given severely reduced EF — critical given the 30 mL/kg crystalloid already administered.
Initial lactate was 4.8 mmol/L (>2 mmol/L), requiring serial measurement per SSC guidelines to guide resuscitation and assess response to treatment.

Patient remains in septic shock with MAP 60, tachycardia HR 105, SpO2 88%, and markedly elevated lactate. Reassess perfusion after fluid resuscitation and vasopressor initiation to evaluate treatment response.

Continuous arterial pressure monitoring is indicated given refractory hypotension (BP 80/50), vasopressor use, and need for frequent blood sampling. Essential for tight hemodynamic management in septic shock with HFrEF EF 15%.

Patient remains hypotensive with MAP of 60 mmHg despite norepinephrine already started. SSC guidelines recommend adding vasopressin as a second vasopressor to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg in refractory septic shock. Patient has HFrEF with EF 15% making adequate perfusion pressure critical.

Central venous access is needed for reliable vasopressor administration (norepinephrine and vasopressin), CVP monitoring, and ongoing resuscitation in this septic shock patient with difficult peripheral access likely given edema.

CBC is indicated to assess WBC count (infection severity), hemoglobin (anemia worsening cardiac output in HFrEF EF 15%), and platelet count (evaluate for DIC given positive blood cultures and coagulopathy risk in septic shock).

Blood cultures are positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae. Identifying the infection source (e.g., pneumonia, meningitis, bacteremia) is critical to guide targeted antibiotic therapy and source control measures.

Patient has septic shock with elevated lactate (4.8) and organ dysfunction. Coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen) are needed to evaluate for DIC, which is common in severe sepsis/septic shock and will guide further management.

Procalcitonin is useful as a biomarker for bacterial infection severity and to guide antibiotic de-escalation decisions. Serial measurements will help monitor response to therapy in this confirmed bacteremic patient.

Patient remains hypotensive (MAP 60 mmHg, BP 80/50) with lactate 4.8 mmol/L and SpO2 88% despite initial 30mL/kg crystalloid bolus and vasopressors. Additional crystalloid fluid administration is indicated per SSC guidelines for ongoing resuscitation in septic shock, while monitoring for fluid responsiveness given the patient's underlying HFrEF with EF 15% and CKD stage 3 (careful titration required).

MANDATORY action — patient remains hypotensive with MAP 60 mmHg (target ≥65 mmHg). Although norepinephrine and vasopressin have been started, this mandatory bundle element must be formally completed per SSC guidelines for septic shock.

Patient has septic shock with persistent hypotension (MAP 60), lactate 4.8, SpO2 88%, dual vasopressor requirement, and complex comorbidities (HFrEF EF 15%, AF, CKD stage 3). ICU admission is required for continuous hemodynamic monitoring and organ support.
